prompt: Which of these is true of a remote MCP server, and not of a local stdio one?

choices.text: It runs as the person who started the host
choices.why: That is a local server.

choices.text: It speaks different messages
choices.why: The messages are the same; the transport changes.

choices.text: It must be told who is asking, on every request
choices.why: Right. A token proves it; a local server's caller is whoever started it.

choices.text: It inherits the host's environment
choices.why: It inherits nothing from the host.

choices.text: Because the network namespace hides other machines' files
choices.why: A namespace separates networks; file access is decided by the owner and mode.

choices.text: The directory belongs to mcpd and is closed to others
choices.why: Right. The server's files, its shop and its token table are mcpd's.

choices.text: Because the server deleted it after starting, so that nothing on disk could be read
choices.why: It was there; ana was refused.

choices.text: Because ana's token lacks a scope
choices.why: Tokens are for the HTTP server, not for files.

prompt: What exit code did curl give when it could not verify the server's certificate?
What made the certificate verify on ana's side?

choices.text: Turning off verification for this host
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson turns verification off.

choices.text: Installing the server's private key
choices.why: The private key never leaves the server.

choices.text: A different port
choices.why: The port is the same.

choices.text: Pointing the client at the lab's CA certificate
choices.why: Right. One file, marginalia-ca.crt.

prompt: What does the WWW-Authenticate header's resource_metadata give a client?

choices.text: The URL of a document naming the server's authorization servers
choices.why: Right. The first link of the discovery chain.

choices.text: A token to retry with
choices.why: No token is handed out by a 401.

choices.text: The list of tools
choices.why: Tools are listed only after authorisation.

choices.text: The server's certificate
choices.why: Certificates are checked during TLS, not through this header.

prompt: Put the discovery chain in order, from the server's address to a token.
items: a request without a token gets 401
the resource metadata names the authorization server
the authorization server's metadata names its endpoints
the client asks for a token

prompt: What did the lab's token endpoint answer, and why?

choices.text: A token, because the lab runs a full authorization server
choices.why: It runs metadata only.

choices.text: 401, because the request had no token
choices.why: The answer was 501.

choices.text: 501: this lab publishes metadata and issues tokens by file
choices.why: Right. The chain is real; issuance is described, not run.

choices.text: Nothing; the port was closed
choices.why: It answered with JSON.

prompt: Why does TokenTable key its table by the token's SHA-256?

choices.text: Because SHA-256 makes lookups faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Because HTTP headers cannot carry a token in clear
choices.why: The header carries the token itself.

choices.text: To make the token shorter on the wire
choices.why: The client still sends the whole token.

choices.text: So it holds no tokens
choices.why: Right. The table itself holds no token, so a copy of it is not a set of working tokens.

prompt: The AuthSettings flag that makes the server refuse tokens issued for another resource is `___`.
Why was the billing token refused, although it was valid and unexpired?

choices.text: It was issued for a different server
choices.why: Right. The audience rule: accept only tokens issued for you.

choices.text: Because its scope was orders:read
choices.why: The support token had the same scope and was accepted.

choices.text: Because billing-agent is on a blocklist the server keeps beside the token table
choices.why: There is no blocklist; the resource did not match.

choices.text: Because it was sent without TLS
choices.why: Every request used TLS.

prompt: Why do the billing and expired tokens get exactly the same 401 body?

choices.text: Because the server could not tell them apart
choices.why: It could; it chose not to say.

choices.text: So that nobody learns which tokens exist or why one fails
choices.why: Right. One answer for every rejected token.

choices.text: Because uvicorn writes all error bodies
choices.why: The SDK's auth middleware writes it.

choices.text: Because both were issued to the same client, old-agent, which the server no longer recognises
choices.why: They were issued to different clients.

prompt: How does the specification recommend answering a valid token whose scope is too narrow?

choices.text: With a tool error inside a 200, as this server does
choices.why: That is what this server does, not what the specification recommends.

choices.text: By granting the scope for one call
choices.why: Servers never widen a token.

choices.text: 403, with WWW-Authenticate naming the scope needed
choices.why: Right. A client then knows which scope to ask for.

choices.text: 401, as for an invalid token
choices.why: 401 is for invalid or expired tokens.

prompt: What did moving a server from local to remote remove from lesson 15's host?

choices.text: The need to check tool results
choices.why: Results still need checking.

choices.text: The audit file
choices.why: The host still writes it.

choices.text: Asking a person before a refund, since the token's scope now decides everything
choices.why: The host's own rules still apply.

choices.text: The ENV list, since the host starts nothing
choices.why: Right. It adds a secret to keep instead: the token.

choices.text: A stolen code being used
choices.why: Right. A stolen authorization code is useless without the client's secret.

choices.text: A server accepting tokens for another resource
choices.why: That is the audience check.

choices.text: Expired tokens
choices.why: Expiry is checked by the server.

choices.text: A server whose certificate was signed by an authority the client does not know
choices.why: That is TLS.

prompt: Which of these does the specification forbid? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: A server passing a client's token on to another service
choices.why: Right. Token passthrough.

choices.text: A client sending a server a token issued for another server
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A server accepting a token not issued for it
choices.why: Right. The audience rule.

choices.text: A client sending its token in the Authorization header
choices.why: That is how tokens are sent.
